Definition: from a compound of G3844 and perhaps a derivative of G3633; apparently a state alongside of supposition, i.e. (concretely) an adage; specially, an enigmatical or fictitious illustration:--parable, proverb.
BiblicalUsage: Paroimia is a proverb, a parable, a dark saying. John uses it for the sayings of Jesus that the disciples do not yet understand: in John 10:6 Jesus speaks a parable to the Pharisees and they do not understand what He says, and in John 16:25 He promises that the time comes when He will speak plainly, no more in proverbs. In John 16:29 the disciples claim they understand at last. Peter borrows a proverb in 2 Peter 2:22: the dog is turned to his own vomit again, and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus spoke in proverbs so that those who would listen would lean in, and the plain speaking comes to those who stay. My position is that the proverb about the dog and the sow is the warning for anyone who returns to what Christ washed away.
